## 1. Load data

```{r setup}
# Install packages once if needed:
# install.packages(c("tidyverse", "broom"))

library(tidyverse)
library(broom)

data_path <- path.expand("~/Downloads/YRBSS_2023_official_cleaned.csv")
if (!file.exists(data_path)) {
  stop("File not found. Update data_path to the location of YRBSS_2023_official_cleaned.csv")
}
raw <- read.csv(data_path)

required <- c("q1", "q2", "q3", "q26", "q27", "q28", "q29", "q76", "q77")
stopifnot(all(required %in% names(raw)))

cat("Total survey respondents:", nrow(raw), "\n")
dir.create("figures", showWarnings = FALSE)
```

## 2. Recode variables

```{r recode}
# CDC codes: Q26-Q28 (1 = Yes, 2 = No); Q29 (1 = 0 attempts, 2-5 = 1+ attempts).
# Q76 codes 1-8 represent 0-7 active days; Q77 codes 1-6 represent 0-5 PE days.

df <- raw %>%
  mutate(
    sad_hopeless = case_when(q26 == 1 ~ 1, q26 == 2 ~ 0, TRUE ~ NA_real_),
    suicide_considered = case_when(q27 == 1 ~ 1, q27 == 2 ~ 0, TRUE ~ NA_real_),
    suicide_planned = case_when(q28 == 1 ~ 1, q28 == 2 ~ 0, TRUE ~ NA_real_),
    suicide_attempted = case_when(q29 == 1 ~ 0, q29 %in% 2:5 ~ 1, TRUE ~ NA_real_),
    phys_act_days = if_else(q76 %in% 1:8, q76 - 1, NA_real_),
    pe_days = if_else(q77 %in% 1:6, q77 - 1, NA_real_),
    activity_group = case_when(
      phys_act_days >= 2 ~ "Active",
      phys_act_days <= 1 ~ "Inactive",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    ),
    activity_group = factor(activity_group, levels = c("Inactive", "Active"))
  )

outcomes <- c("sad_hopeless", "suicide_considered", "suicide_planned", "suicide_attempted")
outcome_names <- c("Sadness/Hopelessness", "Suicidal Ideation", "Suicide Planning", "Suicide Attempts")

# Confirm that all eight physical activity levels are present.
table(df$phys_act_days, useNA = "ifany")
table(df$pe_days, useNA = "ifany")
```

## 3. Sample characteristics and missing data

```{r descriptive}
sex_table <- df %>%
  filter(q2 %in% 1:2) %>%
  count(q2, name = "n") %>%
  mutate(sex = if_else(q2 == 1, "Female", "Male"),
         percent = round(100 * n / sum(n), 1)) %>%
  select(sex, n, percent)

age_table <- df %>%
  filter(q1 %in% 1:7) %>%
  count(q1, name = "n") %>%
  mutate(age = factor(q1, levels = 1:7,
                      labels = c("12 or younger", "13", "14", "15", "16", "17", "18 or older")),
         percent = round(100 * n / sum(n), 1)) %>%
  select(age, n, percent)

# Each outcome is analyzed with its own available cases.
sample_sizes <- tibble(
  outcome = outcome_names,
  n = map_int(outcomes, ~sum(complete.cases(df[, c("phys_act_days", .x)]))),
  missing_outcome = map_int(outcomes, ~sum(is.na(df[[.x]])))
)

print(as.data.frame(sex_table))
print(as.data.frame(age_table))
print(as.data.frame(sample_sizes))
```

## 4. Spearman correlations

```{r correlations}
cor_results <- map_dfr(outcomes, function(y) {
  x <- df %>% filter(!is.na(phys_act_days), !is.na(.data[[y]]))
  test <- cor.test(x$phys_act_days, x[[y]], method = "spearman", exact = FALSE)
  tibble(outcome = y, n = nrow(x), rho = unname(test$estimate), p_value = test$p.value)
}) %>%
  mutate(outcome_label = factor(outcome, levels = outcomes, labels = outcome_names))

print(as.data.frame(cor_results %>% select(outcome_label, n, rho, p_value)))
```

## 5. Active versus inactive: Welch's t-tests

```{r t-tests}
t_results <- map_dfr(outcomes, function(y) {
  x <- df %>% filter(!is.na(activity_group), !is.na(.data[[y]]))
  test <- t.test(reformulate("activity_group", response = y), data = x)
  tibble(
    outcome = y,
    n = nrow(x),
    active_rate = mean(x[[y]][x$activity_group == "Active"]),
    inactive_rate = mean(x[[y]][x$activity_group == "Inactive"]),
    t_statistic = unname(test$statistic),
    p_value = test$p.value
  )
}) %>%
  mutate(
    outcome_label = factor(outcome, levels = outcomes, labels = outcome_names),
    significance = case_when(
      p_value < .001 ~ "***", p_value < .01 ~ "**",
      p_value < .05 ~ "*", TRUE ~ "ns"
    )
  )

print(as.data.frame(t_results %>% select(outcome_label, n, active_rate, inactive_rate, t_statistic, p_value)))
```

## 6. Logistic regression

```{r logistic-regression}
# A separate unadjusted binomial model is fitted for each outcome.
fit_models <- function(predictor) {
  set_names(map(outcomes, ~glm(reformulate(predictor, response = .x),
                               data = df, family = binomial())), outcomes)
}

models_days <- fit_models("phys_act_days")
models_pe <- fit_models("pe_days")
models_group <- fit_models("activity_group")  # Active versus Inactive reference

# Odds ratios and Wald 95% confidence intervals.
get_odds_ratios <- function(models, predictor_name) {
  imap_dfr(models, function(model, y) {
    tidy(model) %>%
      filter(term != "(Intercept)") %>%
      transmute(
        outcome = y,
        predictor = predictor_name,
        n = nobs(model),
        OR = exp(estimate),
        lower = exp(estimate - 1.96 * std.error),
        upper = exp(estimate + 1.96 * std.error),
        p_value = p.value
      )
  })
}

or_days <- get_odds_ratios(models_days, "Additional physical activity day")
or_pe <- get_odds_ratios(models_pe, "Additional PE day")
or_group <- get_odds_ratios(models_group, "Active versus Inactive")
or_results <- bind_rows(or_days, or_pe, or_group) %>%
  mutate(outcome_label = factor(outcome, levels = outcomes, labels = outcome_names))

print(as.data.frame(or_results %>% select(predictor, outcome_label, n, OR, lower, upper, p_value)))
```

## 7. Figure 1: Active versus inactive prevalence

```{r figure-1}
plot_long <- df %>%
  select(phys_act_days, activity_group, all_of(outcomes)) %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = all_of(outcomes), names_to = "outcome", values_to = "response") %>%
  mutate(outcome_label = factor(outcome, levels = outcomes, labels = outcome_names))

group_prevalence <- plot_long %>%
  filter(!is.na(activity_group), !is.na(response)) %>%
  group_by(outcome_label, activity_group) %>%
  summarise(n = n(), prevalence = mean(response), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(
    se = sqrt(prevalence * (1 - prevalence) / n),
    lower = pmax(0, prevalence - 1.96 * se),
    upper = pmin(1, prevalence + 1.96 * se)
  )

star_labels <- group_prevalence %>%
  group_by(outcome_label) %>%
  summarise(y_pos = max(upper) * 1.14, .groups = "drop") %>%
  left_join(t_results %>% select(outcome_label, significance), by = "outcome_label")

fig1 <- ggplot(group_prevalence,
               aes(x = activity_group, y = prevalence, fill = activity_group)) +
  geom_col(width = .68) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = lower, ymax = upper), width = .18) +
  geom_text(data = star_labels,
            aes(x = 1.5, y = y_pos, label = significance),
            inherit.aes = FALSE, size = 5) +
  facet_wrap(~outcome_label, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_x_discrete(limits = c("Active", "Inactive"),
                   labels = c("Active (>=2 days)", "Inactive (<=1 day)")) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Active" = "#EE6561", "Inactive" = "#18AFB4")) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent_format(accuracy = 1),
                     expand = expansion(mult = c(0, .20))) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Prevalence (%)") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(legend.position = "none", strip.text = element_text(face = "bold"),
        axis.text.x = element_text(size = 9))

print(fig1)
ggsave("figures/Figure1_Activity_Groups.png", fig1, width = 10, height = 7, dpi = 600, bg = "white")
ggsave("figures/Figure1_Activity_Groups.pdf", fig1, width = 10, height = 7, bg = "white")
```

## 8. Figure 2: Odds ratios per additional active day

## 9. Figure 3: Prevalence across all 0-7 active days

```{r figure-3}
day_prevalence <- plot_long %>%
  filter(!is.na(phys_act_days), !is.na(response)) %>%
  group_by(outcome_label, phys_act_days) %>%
  summarise(n = n(), prevalence = mean(response), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(
    se = sqrt(prevalence * (1 - prevalence) / n),
    lower = pmax(0, prevalence - 1.96 * se),
    upper = pmin(1, prevalence + 1.96 * se)
  )

cor_labels <- cor_results %>%
  mutate(label = sprintf("Spearman rho = %.3f", rho))

fig3 <- ggplot(day_prevalence, aes(x = phys_act_days, y = prevalence)) +
  geom_line(color = "grey45", linewidth = .7) +
  geom_point(color = "#245A81", size = 2.5) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = lower, ymax = upper),
                color = "#245A81", width = .12) +
  geom_text(data = cor_labels,
            aes(x = 0, y = Inf, label = label),
            inherit.aes = FALSE, hjust = 0, vjust = 1.5, size = 3.5) +
  facet_wrap(~outcome_label, ncol = 2, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 0:7, limits = c(0, 7)) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent_format(accuracy = 1),
                     expand = expansion(mult = c(.08, .20))) +
  labs(x = "Physically active days per week", y = "Prevalence (%)") +
  theme_classic(base_size = 12) +
  theme(strip.background = element_blank(),
        strip.text = element_text(face = "bold"),
        panel.spacing = grid::unit(1.5, "lines"))

print(fig3)
ggsave("figures/Figure3_Daily_Prevalence.png", fig3, width = 10, height = 7, dpi = 600, bg = "white")
ggsave("figures/Figure3_Daily_Prevalence.pdf", fig3, width = 10, height = 7, bg = "white")
```

## 10. Optional Figure 4: Logistic predicted probabilities

```{r figure-4}
# Unlike the observed prevalence in Figure 3, these curves use fitted logistic models.
predicted <- imap_dfr(models_days, function(model, y) {
  new_data <- data.frame(phys_act_days = 0:7)
  p <- predict(model, newdata = new_data, type = "link", se.fit = TRUE)
  tibble(
    outcome = y,
    phys_act_days = 0:7,
    probability = plogis(p$fit),
    lower = plogis(p$fit - 1.96 * p$se.fit),
    upper = plogis(p$fit + 1.96 * p$se.fit)
  )
}) %>%
  mutate(outcome_label = factor(outcome, levels = outcomes, labels = outcome_names))

fig4 <- ggplot(predicted, aes(x = phys_act_days, y = probability)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lower, ymax = upper), fill = "#245A81", alpha = .15) +
  geom_line(color = "#245A81", linewidth = .9) +
  facet_wrap(~outcome_label, ncol = 2, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 0:7) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent_format(accuracy = 1)) +
  labs(x = "Physically active days per week", y = "Predicted probability") +
  theme_classic(base_size = 12) +
  theme(strip.background = element_blank(), strip.text = element_text(face = "bold"))

print(fig4)
ggsave("figures/Figure4_Predicted_Probabilities.png", fig4, width = 10, height = 7, dpi = 600, bg = "white")
ggsave("figures/Figure4_Predicted_Probabilities.pdf", fig4, width = 10, height = 7, bg = "white")
```
